newsitem.title: GERMANY: German labour office refuses budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: German labour office refuses budget cuts.

text.p: Germany's Federal Labour Office refused on Thursday to ratify its 1997 budget in protest at cuts to training and job creation schemes, saying they would only worsen unemployment already at post-unification highs.

A majority of its board rejected a government-imposed budget designed to reduce federal top-up transfers next year to 4.1 billion marks from an earlier planned 9.3 billion, the Labour Office said in a statement.

Bonn wants to batten down costs of jobless pay and makework schemes after rising unemployment caused big spending overruns this year and forced an extra round of budget savings to rein in borrowing next year to qualify for European monetary union.
But, the Labour Office warned, its spending plans are underpinned by an unemployment forecast of 3.9 million next year -- a figure that on current trends looks too low.
It refused further cuts in its budget, saying it would not bear the brunt of failings in government jobs policies.
Following the refusal by the Labour Office to ratify the budget, which foresees spending of 100 billion marks, Labour Minister Norbert Bluem will now have to enforce it.
